title: Affine closed henselian ring presentation
statement: For an affine scheme X and closed immersion i : Z ⟶ X, there exist a small directed preorder I, a ring diagram R : I ⥤ CommRingCat, a colimit cocone c, an ideal K of c.pt with HenselianRing c.pt K, maps t : Spec c.pt ⟶ X and e : Z ≅ Spec(c.pt ⧸ K), and compatible etale maps v a : Spec(R a) ⟶ X presenting t, such that i = e.hom ≫ Spec.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk K) ≫ t. The complete quantified Lean signature, including all coherence equations, is recorded verbatim in lean.statement.

source.place: the affine construction of the henselization and its etale presentation; Tag 0032, construction of a directed final index

proof.text: Set B = Γ(X, top) and x = X.isoSpec. Apply Mathlib IsClosedImmersion.Spec_iff to i composed with x.hom, obtaining an ideal L, an isomorphism z : Z ≅ Spec(B/L), and its exact factorization equation. Apply RingTheory.pair_henselization B L to obtain the essentially small filtered full category P of etale B-algebras with unchanged quotient and its colimit cocone c0 in Under B, with henselian vertex and bijective quotient map.

Pass to J = SmallModel P.FullSubcategory, using equivSmallModel and IsFiltered.of_equivalence. Mathlib IsFiltered.exists_directed gives a nonempty directed partial order I : Type u and a final F : I → J. Compose with the inverse equivalence E to get a final G : I → P.FullSubcategory. Map c0 through Under.forget B; Mathlib Limits.Preserves.Over supplies preservation of filtered colimits. Whisker this ring cocone c along G and use Functor.Final.isColimitWhiskerEquiv to retain its vertex and colimit property. Take the underlying preorder of I.

Put K = L.map c0.pt.hom.hom, t = Spec.map c0.pt.hom composed with x.inv, and q equal to the canonical quotientMap. Convert its bijectivity to the ring isomorphism eq : B/L ≅ c0.pt.right/K, and take e = z followed by Spec of eq inverse. For every b in B, quotientMap_mk gives mk_K(eta(b)) = eq(mk_L(b)). Thus eta followed by mk_K followed by eq.inv equals mk_L. Contravariant functoriality of Spec, the equation from Spec_iff, and cancellation of x prove the required factorization of i. Define v(a) = Spec.map (G.obj a).obj.hom followed by x.inv. Under-morphism commutativity for G.map f and c0.ι.app (G.obj a) proves both compatibility equations after applying Spec.map_comp. Etaleness is the defining property of each object of P followed by an isomorphism. No argument requires L to be proper or nonzero.

lean.statement:
theorem Etale.affine_closed_henselian_ring_presentation
    {X Z : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)) (_ : Nonempty I)
      (R : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (c : Cocone R) (_ : IsColimit c)
      (K : Ideal c.pt) (_ : HenselianRing c.pt K)
      (t : Spec c.pt ⟶ X) (e : Z ≅ Spec (.of (c.pt ⧸ K))),
      i = e.hom ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk K)) ≫ t ∧
      ∃ v : ∀ a : I, Spec (R.obj a) ⟶ X,
        (∀ (a b : I) (f : a ⟶ b), v b = Spec.map (R.map f) ≫ v a) ∧
        (∀ a : I, t = Spec.map (c.ι.app a) ≫ v a) ∧
        (∀ a : I, Etale (v a))
